name: Claude Desktop
intro: Claude Desktop runs the PyPI package with `uv`, so no server has to be started. Add this to `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` (macOS) or `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json` (Windows) and restart Claude Desktop. You can also install the `.mcpb` file attached to each GitHub release as an extension.

alt.label: Alternative: connect to an HTTP server that is already running (needs Node.js 18+ for `mcp-remote`)

name: Claude Code
intro: One command and you are set: Claude Code starts the server over stdio with `uvx`. Restart the session to see the tools.
code: claude mcp add ecuador-datos -- uvx ecuador-mcp --transport stdio

alt.label: Alternative: an HTTP server that is already running
alt.code: claude mcp add --transport http ecuador-datos http://localhost:8000/mcp

name: HTTP / Docker
intro: For remote clients or your own deployments. Docker requires a token (`MCP_AUTH_TOKEN`); the endpoint is `http://localhost:8000/mcp`. Without Docker, `uv run` serves it on the same port.
code:
MCP_AUTH_TOKEN="$(openssl rand -hex 32)" docker compose up -d
# or, without Docker:
uv sync && uv run python main.py --transport http --port 8000

name: Codex
intro: Saves the configuration to `~/.codex/config.toml` (an `[mcp_servers.ecuador-datos]` block with `url`). To use the server over stdio instead of HTTP: `codex mcp add ecuador-datos -- uvx ecuador-mcp --transport stdio`.

name: HuggingChat
